status: Review study after user rejected both v1 appearance and movement; not integrated into Unity.
prompts:
Use case: identity-preserve + 2D animation sprite sheet.
Create a NEW high-quality frame-by-frame RUN CYCLE for ONLY character C, the rightmost character in the attached reference sheet. Reference is the visual identity, especially the LOWER RIGHT running pose. Do not use A or B. Preserve C's broad asymmetric single wrapping cloak and two long trailing panels, large round ivory head with one tiny black eye, hidden neck, short arms and very short legs. Improve softness with curved flowing contours and quiet matte paper shading. This must look like a graceful mysterious 2D metroidvania hero, not a plastic doll, not a 3D render, not a feathered Christmas-tree costume. NO stack of scalloped triangular plates, no three-tier cape; one broad front wrap with two soft trailing tails. Short shins mostly concealed. Head approximately 43% of upright height.
OUTPUT: one production animation sheet, landscape 1536x1024, EXACTLY 12 complete separate sprites, laid out 4 columns by 3 rows, chronological reading order left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Invisible equal 384x341 cells. Each character fits inside its cell with 24+ px clear margins, entire cloak and feet visible. TRUE TRANSPARENT alpha background, no painted checkerboard, no ground, no shadows outside the body, no text, numbers, borders, gutters or title.
All frames face RIGHT, strict fixed orthographic side view, NOT rotating toward camera. EXACT SAME head shape, eye location, size, palette, costume and camera scale across all 12. Position the hip at the same horizontal anchor in each cell. A virtual ground baseline at 84% of cell height. This is RUNNING IN PLACE for animation; no horizontal translation across cells.
POSE QUALITY OVERRIDES EVERYTHING: whole body leans forward 18 degrees, head over leading knee, shoulders and hips respond to each footfall. Draw true bent knees and elbows, never shear or stretch limbs like rubber sticks. Distinct contact / compression / passing / toe-off / flight / descending poses. Two visible tiny feet when silhouette permits, no extra limbs.
Frames 1..6 are first step: 1 right foot forward contacting ground, left leg bent behind; 2 weight settles onto right bent knee and body drops slightly; 3 right planted foot passes under hip, left knee swings forward; 4 right toes push off behind, left knee raised in front; 5 short flight, both feet off ground, left leg reaching ahead and right leg tucked behind, body rises subtly; 6 descending with left foot reaching for ground.
Frames 7..12 repeat same six phases with LEFT and RIGHT legs exchanged: 7 left foot contacts front, 8 compress left knee, 9 left foot under hip while right knee advances, 10 left toe-off and right knee forward, 11 flight/right reach, 12 descent/right reach leading naturally back to frame 1. The nearer leg and hand stay ivory, the far leg and hand are slightly darker gray for legibility.
The cloak MUST visibly stream backward (LEFT), joining at shoulders, curving with one broad wave. Shoulder attachment follows the torso; tail tips lag about one or two drawn frames, first curving down then lifting through passing/flight, never remaining a rigid triangle. As the torso compresses, the cloth bunches gently at the collar; on push-off it lengthens backward. Limit motion so cloak length/shape stays recognizably C and not wild wind. Tiny front hand swings opposite front leg near chest, not broad flailing.
Material: 2D painted cut-paper illustration with broad controlled ivory and graphite-gray value masses; very subtle low-contrast paper texture anchored to the form; soft matte contour lighting, no photorealistic spherical shading, no over-detailed crumpled foil texture. Stable flat lighting. The user rejected the previous version because both design and motion felt unnatural: this must be coherent purposeful running with a flowing long cloak, not a stationary torso with wiggling attached limbs.
Create all 12 frames carefully with constant character dimensions and obvious advancing gait phases. Transparent sprite sheet only.

Edit this exact 12-frame running sprite sheet. Keep ALL 12 existing full-body running poses, their limb anatomy, original compact proportions, frame ordering, scale, head and eye positions, individual frame placement, and 4-column by 3-row layout. One targeted change: the user says SOFTNESS is the most important thing. Remove ALL tiny zigzag tears and sawtooth nicks from the cloak hems, replacing them with broad smooth gently rounded continuous curves. Round the rear tips slightly and use very broad shallow uneven curves, never jagged confetti or spikes. Keep the long broad asymmetric body-wrapping front panel and two flowing rear tails, their folds, their overlaps and changing flow in each existing running pose. Reduce paper grain contrast by 35 percent, retaining a quiet matte paper feel and broad graphite-gray inner folds. Absolutely do NOT create short scalloped layers or feathers. Preserve the 2D ivory character and one tiny black dot eye. Slightly quieter soft illustrated values rather than glossy spherical 3D shading. TRUE TRANSPARENT alpha background, absolutely no opaque background or external glow, no painted checkerboard, labels or borders. Same canvas 1536x1024 and same twelve sprites in the exact same cells. Refine contour softness only, do not reorganize, add poses or change identities.
output: 12 full-body run poses, alpha PNGs, 24 fps run study, side-by-side browser preview
method: Whole-body artwork generated as poses, followed by mechanical crop, uniform scale and translation registration; no synthesized or warped inbetweens.
limitations: Pose/cloth continuity and grounded foot motion are not production validated. Existing Unity v1 is rejected and must not be treated as approved.
